# sherpa-quick-filter

A filter chip used in toolbars. Figma "Filter Chip (atom)" (154:3904), State axis simple \| menu.

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Category | control |
| Figma | Filter Chip (atom) |
| Source | [.ts](../../src/components/sherpa-quick-filter/sherpa-quick-filter.ts) · [.html](../../src/components/sherpa-quick-filter/sherpa-quick-filter.html) · [.css](../../src/components/sherpa-quick-filter/sherpa-quick-filter.css) · [.component.json](../../src/components/sherpa-quick-filter/sherpa-quick-filter.component.json) · [.example.json](../../src/components/sherpa-quick-filter/sherpa-quick-filter.example.json) |

## Example

```html
<sherpa-quick-filter data-label="Unassigned"></sherpa-quick-filter>
<sherpa-quick-filter data-label="Region" data-menu><sherpa-menu slot="menu" data-heading="Region" data-select="multiple"><label><input type="checkbox" value="emea" /> EMEA</label><label><input type="checkbox" value="apac" /> APAC</label></sherpa-menu></sherpa-quick-filter>
```

## Attributes

| Attribute | Values | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-label` | text |  | the name of a chip that shows no label. Its tooltip says it. TRAP T-a-chip-says-its-own-answer |
| `data-applied-at` | text |  |  |
| `data-column` | text |  | which column a group or sort chip arranges by, for a host that draws the choice without a menu. A menu, where there is one, is the answer. |
| `data-condition` | `simple` `advanced` |  | written BY the chip: simple \| advanced — which condition it holds, absent when it holds none. No colour follows it: an Advanced chip is active, as a Simple one. TRAP T-a-conditioned-chip-reads-as-active |
| `data-count` | text |  | leading count chip (shown when present). A menu sets it only at TWO or more picked values — at one the label already names the value, so a "1" badge would be noise. Hovering the badge reveals .count-tip ABOVE it, listing the chosen values. The bubble is a local copy of the [sherpa-tooltip](sherpa-tooltip.md) look rather than a nested instance: the badge lives in this shadow root, so a light-DOM wrapper component cannot reach it. Reveal is pure CSS on .count-wrap:hover. |
| `data-current` | boolean | `false` | selected/on state |
| `data-direction` | `asc` `desc` |  | asc \| desc — which way a sort chip POINTS. `data-current` says whether it runs, so a suspended sort resumes the way it was. TRAP T-off-is-not-forgotten |
| `data-dismiss` | boolean |  | its right button DISMISSES — a cross, not a caret — and reports `quick-filter-dismiss`. The Saved chip. TODO 105 |
| `data-full-value` | boolean |  |  |
| `data-icon` | text |  | start leading icon — an FA class list (Figma default is a funnel) |
| `data-icon-only` | boolean |  | the chip reduced to JUST its menu button — a 24 square with a funnel. Body, count, indicator and value label are all hidden in CSS. For a filter affordance whose field is named elsewhere (a data-grid column header). |
| `data-icon-start` | text |  | leading icon — an icon name (Figma default is a funnel) |
| `data-id` | text |  |  |
| `data-indicator` | boolean |  | show the leading status dot (Figma "Indicator (atom)", opt-in) |
| `data-kind` | `boolean` `single` `multi` `advanced` `number` `date` `group` `sort` |  | WHAT THIS CHIP IS: group \| sort \| advanced. Group and sort ARRANGE rows rather than choosing them, so they have no values to be empty of, and both own their gesture — group toggles, sort cycles asc / desc / off — and report it themselves. "Organise" is not a kind; it is a heading a panel may draw above the two. TRAP T-a-chip-knows-what-kind-it-is `advanced` with no filter menu is a SAVED filter: its answer is given, so the chip is a toggle that reads as Advanced. TRAP T-a-saved-filter-is-its-readings |
| `data-label` | text |  | chip text (or use the default slot). Rewritten to "Field: Value" while exactly ONE menu value is picked; two or more revert to the field name plus the count badge. |
| `data-locked` | boolean |  |  |
| `data-menu` | boolean | `false` | Figma State=menu — snap on the caret button |
| `data-no-value` | boolean |  |  |
| `data-open` | boolean |  |  |
| `data-panelled` | boolean |  | a FILTER PANEL is drawing this field instead, so the bar hides the chip — two controls over one field make a reader guess which is in force. Written by the host. TRAP T-the-view-chip-stays-on-the-header |
| `data-pending` | boolean |  | changed, not yet applied: the active edge, no fill. Written by the bar. TRAP T-a-pending-chip-has-no-fill |
| `data-persistent` | boolean |  | a SELECTOR rather than a toggle: always on, and never "empty". Set by [sherpa-quick-filter-toolbar](sherpa-quick-filter-toolbar.md) from a filter definition's `persistent` flag. The view chip is the case — you are always in SOME view, so the amber "on but filtering by nothing" state is one it cannot be in. |
| `data-plain` | boolean |  |  |
| `data-readonly` | boolean |  | a KEY, not a control: no toggle, no button semantics. TRAP T-readonly-legend-is-a-key-not-a-filter |
| `data-superseded` | boolean |  |  |
| `data-swatch` | text |  | a data-viz series, from 1, or a status name: the chip leads with that swatch, as a chart's legend does — one value of a chart's own filter. TRAP T-a-chart-scope-is-its-legend-field |
| `data-type` | `default` `ai` `jump` `key` |  | default \| ai \| jump \| key `jump` is a JUMP TO chip, not a filter: never on. Its menu lists places on the page, filled by populate([{ value, label }]); a pick scrolls the element whose id is `value` into view. `key` is a chart legend's row: no border, mono 12px, 16 tall. Its ON is SHOWN, so at rest every key is on. TODO 149 |
| `data-unavailable` | boolean |  | the other filters rule this value out: greyed, refused, and its tooltip says why. Written by the host. TRAP T-a-ruled-out-value-is-greyed |
| `data-unsupported` | boolean |  |  |
| `disabled` | boolean, native | `false` | greyed and refused; its tooltip says "Not available here." |

## Methods

| Method | What it does |
|---|---|
| `clear(op: FilterOp = DEFAULT_OP)` | clear(op) — EMPTY the chip, whatever answers it, and switch it off: a list's ticks, typing and rows, a number's two shapes, a date's days. SILENT. `op` is the condition a list goes back to. |
| `arrangeBy(field: string, direction?: string \| null)` | arrangeBy(field, direction) — steer a GROUP or SORT chip: its column, and for a sort which way. SILENT, like every steer. No field is OFF, and the chip keeps the column it had; a sort with `''` for its direction is suspended, and resumes ascending. The CHIP's own, so a bar and a panel follow the same attributes the same way. |
| `toggleMenu(anchor?: HTMLElement)` | Open or shut this chip's menu — what a HOST calls to drive the chip from outside. It routes through the same light-dismiss-safe path a caret click takes, so an external opener cannot get the stuck-open behaviour back. |
| `refresh()` | refresh() — redraw the FACE (value, tip, badge, condition) off the menu, once its rows have filled. For a host that set the rows SILENTLY: a steer fires no menu event, so the chip never heard it and kept a stale face. Never on or off — that stays the host's. |

## Events

Each one bubbles.

| Event | Detail | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| `quick-filter-click` | `{ active: boolean }` | The chip body is toggled. |
| `quick-filter-change` | `{ scope: 'chip'; values: string[] }` | The menu selection changed. |
| `quick-filter-dismiss` |  | A data-dismiss chip's right button was pressed. |
| `jump-select` | `{ label: string; value: string }` | A jump row was picked, and its target scrolled into view. |
| `group-change` | `{ field: null \| string }` | A GROUP chip picked or cleared its column. |
| `sort-change` | `{ direction: SortDirection; field: null \| string }` | A SORT chip picked its column or way. |

|---|---|---|

| `menu` | menu | a &lt;[sherpa-menu](sherpa-menu.md)> of values for this field |

## populate()

`[{ value, label }]`

a JUMP chip's places, as action rows in its menu. Any other chip keeps the default: payload keys onto its attributes.
